sections.h2: Highland Park housing at a glance
sections.html:
Highland Park sits in Lake County on the North Shore, about 25 miles north of downtown Chicago. The city is split between Moraine Township and West Deerfield Township, and mail runs through ZIP codes 60035, 60036 and 60037. Population is 30,767 in the mid-2025 estimate.

Lake Michigan shapes the layout. A bluff about 100 feet high runs along 6 miles of shoreline, and wooded ravines cut up to a mile inland. A house beside a ravine or at the bluff edge sells differently from one on a flat street near a Metra stop, and buyers will ask about the lot as closely as the building.

The five-year survey figures for 2020 to 2024 show 11,787 households, 83.8 percent of them owner-occupied, with a median home value of $607,300 and a median gross rent of $1,925. About 87.5 percent of residents stayed at the same address through the previous year, which describes a city of long-time owners.

sections.h2: Older homes and what buyers ask for
sections.html:
The city was platted in 1856 after the Chicago and Milwaukee Railroad built a depot, and it became a city on March 11, 1869. That early start left a lot of older houses. The Willits House is on the federal historic register, and the register also lists work by Frank Lloyd Wright, John S. Van Bergen, Howard Van Doren Shaw, Robert E. Seyfarth and David Adler.

If you own an architect-designed house, you probably have the original plans, permits and drawings somewhere. Gather them before you talk to any buyer. Documented history is one of the few things that can set a house apart from its neighbors.

  • Most residents stay put, so your listing may be the first on the street in years. Pull recent sale records before you pick a price.
  • Older construction makes for a long inspection report, and a buyer may ask to see plans and permits.
  • Four Metra stations inside city limits make distance to the platform a selling point for downtown workers.

North Shore School District 112 runs the elementary and middle schools. Township High School District 113 runs Highland Park High School and also Deerfield High School in nearby Deerfield.

US 41 is the main highway and connects Chicago to Milwaukee. The four Metra stations are Braeside, Ravinia Park, Ravinia and Highland Park, all on the Union Pacific North Line. Pace buses add local routes, O'Hare is about 20 miles southwest, and the Skokie Valley Trail runs through town. Three public beaches, Rosewood, Moraine and Park Avenue, line the shore. Buyers of every type, cash buyers included, weigh the stations, schools and beaches when they set a price.

sections.h2: What the city requires before closing
sections.html:
Chapter 97, Article X of the city code taxes real property transfers. The declaration form prints the rate as $5.00 per $1,000 or fraction thereof of full actual consideration, and it puts payment on the transferor when the sale contract says nothing different.

  • The declaration needs a signature from a transferor and a transferee.
  • A final water bill must be prepared and paid when the tax stamp is bought, and a final meter reading can be scheduled up to five business days before closing.
  • A copy of the deed headed for the Recorder of Deeds goes to the city, while an exempt transfer requires the original.
  • Consideration counts the mortgage amount and any liabilities the buyer assumes.
  • Section 97.1004 lists exempt deeds, such as tax deeds, partition deeds, deeds with consideration under $100, and foreclosure or in-lieu deeds to a mortgage holder.

Personal checks and credit cards are refused. Finance, at 1707 St. Johns Avenue, takes calls at 847.432.0800 and email at Finance@cityhpil.com. Ask for the final water reading early so closing does not wait on a meter.

sections.h2: Recording the deed with Lake County
sections.html:
The Recording Division of the Lake County Clerk's Office handles deeds at 18 N County Street, 6th Floor, Waukegan, phone 847-377-2575. The fee is $70 for a standard document and $82 for a non-standard one, and state and county transfer taxes are the only added charges at recording.

The state levies its own tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-10, charged on the value stated in the declaration, and a mortgage the buyer takes over can be excluded when the deed says so. Your closing agent will give you the county rate and a final total.

sections.h2: A step-by-step order for the sale
sections.html:
Most Highland Park sales follow the same order, whichever route you pick. Knowing it ahead of time keeps a closing date from slipping over paperwork.

  1. Settle on a route and sign a contract that says who pays the transfer charges.
  2. Fill out the city declaration. Both a transferor and a transferee must sign it.
  3. Ask the city to schedule the final meter reading, which can happen up to five business days before closing.
  4. Pay the final water bill and buy the tax stamp at Finance. Bring a payment other than a personal check or a credit card.
  5. Have the closing agent prepare the deed and compute the state and county transfer taxes from the value stated in the declaration.
  6. File the deed with the Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan and send the city its copy.

If your house is on a ravine lot or a bluff, or was designed by a known architect, hand the buyer the plans and permits early. A buyer with documents in hand tends to ask fewer questions at the end, and that helps a short closing hold together. Keep copies of everything you sign for your own files.

sections.h2: Which selling route fits a Highland Park owner in a hurry?
sections.html:
Three routes exist, and each trades price, certainty and effort differently.

  • Work with a listing agent. Exposure is widest, and a bluff, ravine or architect-designed property can justify a longer wait.
  • Sell on your own. You control the contract and carry the showings, disclosures and negotiation.
  • Accept a cash offer. The closing date can follow your calendar and the house stays as it is, which helps with an estate home, a tenant-occupied unit or a house that needs work.

The city stamp, the final water bill and the deed filing apply on every route. When a cash buyer makes an offer, get in writing who pays each transfer charge named above. The sale contract is where that split is settled, so read it before you sign.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and the loan approval wait, and you can usually choose a closing date that suits a move or an estate timeline.

faqs.q: How many people live in Highland Park?
faqs.a: The April 2020 census found 30,176 residents, and the mid-2025 estimate is 30,767.

faqs.q: Who owes the city transfer tax on a Highland Park sale?
faqs.a: The transferor does, unless the sale contract says otherwise.

faqs.q: Does a Highland Park sale need a final water bill?
faqs.a: Yes. It must be prepared and paid when the stamp is bought, and a final meter reading can be booked up to five business days ahead of closing.

faqs.q: Which office files the deed after a Highland Park closing?
faqs.a: The Lake County Clerk's Recording Division in Waukegan. The fee for a standard document is $70.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Highland Park?
faqs.a: North Shore School District 112 runs the elementary and middle schools, and Township High School District 113 runs Highland Park High School and Deerfield High School.
